trigger: The drive letter of a planned Program Files root is re-pointed or swapped (SUBST, disk management, hot-plug) during the up-to-45 s scan window
policy_floor: runtimes row clause 1 (DRIVE_FIXED only, checked at open) applied as the owner-directed standard
summary: DRIVE_FIXED is tested once at root planning (is_fixed_drive via plan_windows_targets) and never at open time: list_directory and open_regular_file open by drive letter through the root handle with no GetDriveTypeW. The runtimes leg re-checks per read (runtimes_win_parsers.hpp:348). Banner at component_fs_win.cpp:26 'Only DRIVE_FIXED volumes are walked' is not enforced at open. Exposure is narrow (needs admin or physical control, race), recommended fix is three lines; arguable for adjudication but the derivation and the runtimes clause both gate it

trigger: ProgramFilesDir or ProgramFilesDir (x86) redirected to a UNC or otherwise non-drive path (verified on the pure layer: x64=\\srv\share, x86=C:\PF86 gives roots=1, roots_network_skipped=0, mount_table_unreadable=false); or GetDriveTypeW UNKNOWN/NO_ROOT_DIR for a Program Files drive
policy_floor: runtimes row clause 2 (a failed or skipped read is a token and CONSTRAINED, never an empty supported) applied as the owner-directed standard
summary: windows_candidate_roots drops a UNC, relative or bare-root candidate with no count and no token, so the answer is supported/FULL with a Program Files tree never walked (silent). Separately plan_windows_targets counts a drive whose type could not be told as network_fs_skipped (informational), so an all-dropped host answers supported with zero rows. README:26 and ADR-0028 document the second case; the first is undocumented. One fix covers both: count every dropped candidate (UNC as roots_network_skipped, unreadable type or unnameable path as mount_table_unreadable)

trigger: A Windows host with Compact OS (WOF) or cloud placeholders in Program Files: candidate DLLs/JARs carry FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT
summary: A candidate file stored behind a reparse point is typed link and never read; the answer stays supported and link_skipped carries no count or cause, so a skipped DLL reads like a junction (README discloses it). Possible tension with runtimes clause 2; owner decision on a separate token or CONSTRAINED. The real Windows capture settles whether WOF files report the attribute in directory records (not run here)

trigger: A Windows host without Program Files (x86) (for example Server Core without WoW64)
summary: Both known-folder lookups must answer, and a root that does not exist reads as dir_unreadable/mount_table_unreadable, so the answer is permanently constrained with a token whose README advice (check permissions) is wrong. Behaviour on such a host unverified; settle with the capture

trigger: A refactor drops scan_policy(t)/native_policy(nt) in the plugin or swaps the Windows candidate/parser selection
summary: The plugin's WindowsApps wiring (anonymous-namespace scan_policy/native_policy) is observed only by the hidden Windows host-walk case, which skips its token and pe checks when the 45 s or entry budget hits first; no cross-OS test covers it. Header mutation note states the limit honestly (not a false-green). Fix: move both builders into component_legs_win.hpp and test on every OS

trigger: A user creates a file named with a lone surrogate (for example lone\uD800) in a writable Program Files subdirectory
summary: No test takes a WTF-8 lone-surrogate name through format_component_row to see '?' (wire_field/scrub_wire_bytes rejects ED A0..BF per wire_utf8.hpp:43; the host also scrubs plugin output). The security pass fuzzed the encoder and scrub path and found no defect. One cross-OS case

trigger: An antivirus or backup agent holds an exclusive lock on a DLL during the native walk (sharing violation on open)
summary: open_regular_file returns nullopt on any open failure, which the scan reports as the archive_changed cause: the token misnames a sharing violation and the whole native answer goes constrained, rows kept. Not exercised on Windows (deferred capture)

trigger: A dead or hung fixed volume parks NtCreateFile, GetFileInformationByHandleEx or ReadFile; the 45 s wall budget is checked only between directories and files
summary: No per-call deadline; one command thread-pool worker (agent.cpp:4100, 4-32 threads) is occupied, not the stream, heartbeat or sync threads. Disclosed in the source banner, README caveat 2, ADR-0028 and the runtimes row clause 1 (disclosed residual, same primitive), so it matches the standard; a fix is an independent surface (worker/timeout design) shared with runtimes

trigger: A later flag change lands in one of two hand-copied NtCreateFile bodies
summary: open_dir_no_reparse copies about 25 lines of open_file_no_reparse. No MUST in a routed row requires a single copy. Gate 0 ponytail r1 ruled keep as is (ad31396d7e). Maintainability only

Fixed in the governance r1 round: the drive type is asked again before every directory open (list_directory) and every file open (open_regular_file) through the pure volume_is_fixed gate over GetDriveTypeW, and anything but a fixed answer (not fixed or unknown) is a refused open on the existing error path (dir_unreadable, or a changed archive). Pure tests pin the gate and the drive classes on every OS; a Windows-only case stages fixed, then not fixed, on one leg over a real tree.

Fixed in the governance r1 round: every candidate root is walked, counted or constraining. A UNC path counts in roots_network_skipped; a path that names no walkable directory, or a drive whose type cannot be told (UNKNOWN, NO_ROOT_DIR), sets mount_table_unreadable; only a network, removable, optical or RAM drive is the informational network_fs_skipped. README and ADR-0028 now say so. Pure tests cover each cause and the status row of an all-dropped host.
